summary: Both grammar flags are plain adjectives (`verbaasde` is even named as fine in restricted.md) and the load finding is a segmentation artefact. Two must_fix: the B2 dialogue-tag verb `kaatste terug` and the disjointed `Het is goed, zo’n ontmoeting: iemand kent zijn plaats.` The literary starting point shows in the load: a 22-word opening sentence with an 11-word subject, an em-dash aside that splits subject and verb in b062, and two calques (`rekten zijn lippen zich uit`, `Mijn hart valt flauw`); `zo nu en dan` is a B1 phrase the tool did not see and pushes the stretch budget over. Vocabulary choices are otherwise the best of the three (no gloss on `eer`, `handdruk` glossed, `schenkt` for the smile).

findings.fragment: \gl{kaatste}{lobbed} de andere jongen terug
findings.problem: `terugkaatsen` is a B2 verb used once as a dialogue tag; a plain verb carries the same information.
findings.evidence: lexicon: kaatsen hard B2 (glossed); one-off narrator flourish, not a world term and not recurring
findings.required_fix: Replace the tag with `antwoordde de andere jongen, met een glimlach` and drop the gloss (remove the `kaatste terug` line from @glosses).

findings.fragment: Het is goed, zo’n ontmoeting: iemand kent zijn plaats.
findings.problem: The colon sentence is disjointed: `zo’n ontmoeting` has nothing to point at, and `iemand kent zijn plaats` as a bare main clause reads as a statement about some unknown person, not as 'someone who knows his place'; a native reader re-reads it.
findings.evidence: NL: 'Het is goed, zo’n ontmoeting: iemand kent zijn plaats.' — no Dutch ellipsis pattern supports this
findings.required_fix: Use one allowed als-clause (A-SUB): `Het is fijn als iemand zijn plaats kent.`

findings.fragment: Naast Harry was een bleke jongen met een spits gezicht en \emph{supercool} witblond haar in de laatste fase van hetzelfde proces, zo leek het.
findings.problem: 22 words in one clause; the reader must hold `was` across an 11-word subject before the predicate `in de laatste fase` arrives, and `zo leek het` trails after everything.
findings.evidence: L-LEN soft limit 20; copula and predicate separated by 11 words (L-FRAME spirit)
findings.required_fix: Split: `Naast Harry stond een bleke jongen met een spits gezicht en \emph{supercool} witblond haar. Hij was, zo leek het, in de laatste fase van hetzelfde proces.`

findings.fragment: Een van de assistentes—zij herkende Harry eerder al, zo leek het—maakte een zacht, \gl{verstikt}{choked} geluid.
findings.problem: An em-dash aside with two finite verbs of its own sits between the subject and its verb; three finite verbs and an interrupted main clause is the hardest pattern for this profile even though no subordinator is used.
findings.evidence: finite verbs herkende / leek / maakte = 3 (limit); subject `Een van de assistentes` is 9 words away from `maakte`
findings.required_fix: Two sentences in time order: `Een van de assistentes herkende Harry eerder al, zo leek het. Zij maakte nu een zacht, \gl{verstikt}{choked} geluid.`

findings.fragment: Toen rekten zijn lippen zich uit tot een \gl{zelfvoldane}{smug} glimlach.
findings.problem: `zich uitrekken` is what a body or a cat does; applied to lips it is a word-for-word copy of 'his lips stretched'.
findings.evidence: NL 'rekten zijn lippen zich uit' vs idiomatic 'er kwam een glimlach op zijn lippen'
findings.required_fix: `Toen kwam er een brede, \gl{zelfvoldane}{smug} glimlach op zijn lippen.` (presentational er, A-ER-NEW)

findings.fragment: Mijn hart valt flauw.
findings.problem: `flauwvallen` is something people do; 'my heart faints' is a literal rendering of 'swoon' that a Dutch reader hears as odd rather than as Harry's purple prose.
findings.evidence: NL 'Mijn hart valt flauw.' — no Dutch collocation; `mijn hart smelt` is the idiom with the same flirty ring b064 needs
findings.required_fix: `Mijn hart smelt.`

findings.fragment: Zo nu en dan tikte ze
findings.problem: `zo nu en dan` is a B1 phrase in the lexicon (not surfaced by the tool); with it the unglossed stretch items are 4 (frustratie, babbelen, verdomme, zo nu en dan) against a budget of 3, and `af en toe` (A1) means exactly the same.
findings.evidence: lexicon phrases: 'zo nu en dan' stretch B1; 'af en toe' known A1
findings.required_fix: `Af en toe tikte ze met haar \gl{toverstok}{wand} tegen een hoek van het gewaad, …`

findings.fragment: met een licht verbaasde blik
findings.problem: `licht` as 'slightly' is a known word in a new sense; `een beetje verbaasd` is more transparent, but the phrase is natural and `verbaasd` is A1.
findings.evidence: lexicon: licht known A2 (ADJ/NOUN 'light'); flag R-PARTICIPLE dismissed
findings.required_fix: Optional: `zei Draco Malfidus, een beetje verbaasd.`

findings.fragment: besloot hij: de maat is vol.
findings.problem: Idiom of known words whose meaning is not compositional ('the measure is full'); the colon and `besloot` carry the reader, but `genoeg is genoeg` is transparent.
findings.evidence: lexicon: maat A1, vol A2; phrase not in the lexicon
findings.required_fix: Keep if the meaning reviewer is happy; otherwise `genoeg is genoeg`.

findings.fragment: meestal rond dit punt
findings.problem: `rond dit punt` for a moment in time is a mild calque of 'at around this point'.
findings.evidence: NL 'kwamen de tranen meestal rond dit punt'
findings.required_fix: Optional: `Bij de anderen kwamen de tranen meestal op dit moment.`

findings.fragment: kon maar moeilijk zijn volgende tekst bedenken
findings.problem: `maar` in its 'only' sense and `tekst` in the actor's sense are known words in new senses; natural Dutch, slightly less transparent than `kon niet meteen een volgende zin bedenken`.
findings.evidence: lexicon: maar A1 'but'; tekst A1 'text'
findings.required_fix: Optional: `Harry kon niet meteen zijn volgende zin bedenken.`

findings.fragment: bekeek de jongen met het witte haar en zijn \gl{gewaad}{robe} met een patroon als een schaakbord
findings.problem: Two `met`-phrases in a row; readable, but the separate sentence of V1 (`Het gewaad had een patroon van vierkanten, net als een schaakbord.`) is lighter.
findings.evidence: 20 words, one clause
findings.required_fix: Optional, only if b055 is reworked anyway.

findings.fragment: tot een \gl{handdruk}{handshake}
findings.problem: B2 in the lexicon but a transparent compound (`hand` + `druk`), glossed; b066 carries two glosses, the limit.
findings.evidence: vocab table: handdruk hard B2, glossed
findings.required_fix: Keep.

findings.fragment: \emph{supercool} witblond haar
findings.problem: Flagged unknown, but `super` (A2) + the loanword `cool` is transparent, and the bible fixes 'awesomecool' → *supercool*.
findings.evidence: vocab table: supercool unknown; bible ch 5 decision
findings.required_fix: None. Lexicon owner: add `supercool` as known.

findings.fragment: witblond
findings.problem: Flagged unknown; compound of `wit` (A1) + `blond` (A1).
findings.evidence: vocab table: witblond unknown (tagged NOUN)
findings.required_fix: None. Lexicon owner: add `witblond` as known; the b055 cluster disappears together with L14.

findings.fragment: als flirten met Draco of zo
findings.problem: Flagged unknown; international loanword, transparent for the reader.
findings.evidence: vocab table: flirten unknown
findings.required_fix: None. Lexicon owner: add `flirten` as known.

findings.fragment: \gl{zelfvoldane}{smug} glimlach
findings.problem: Not in the lexicon, but it is Draco's recurring smile; the plain words (`tevreden`, `trots`) lose the smugness.
findings.evidence: glossed; recurs in later chapters
findings.required_fix: Keep glossed (first occurrence per chapter).

findings.fragment: \gl{verrukt}{delighted} … Gewoon onuitsprekelijk verrukt
findings.problem: Rare word, but it is the mock-courtly register the joke needs; `dolblij` (A2) is the plain fallback if a gloss slot is ever needed.
findings.evidence: glossed once, repeated once; b063 has exactly two glosses
findings.required_fix: Keep. (The tool counted it twice, as `verrukt` and `verrukken`.)

findings.fragment: \gl{onuitsprekelijk}{unutterably}
findings.problem: Rare, but it is the joke word and `on-uit-spreek-lijk` is decodable from known parts.
findings.evidence: glossed
findings.required_fix: Keep glossed.

findings.fragment: wilt u zich dan misschien \gl{verwaardigen}{deign} tot een \gl{handdruk}{handshake}
findings.problem: Very formal reflexive verb + `tot`; heavy but legal (modal + bare infinitive), and it is the 'deign' joke with no plain equivalent of the same register. `Niets wens ik liever:` after it is fronted-object inversion (A-INV), fine.
findings.evidence: glossed; no te-infinitive
findings.required_fix: Keep glossed.

findings.fragment: frustratie (b057), babbelde (b063), Verdomme (b066); verstikt (b062) and onderdanen (b065) glossed
findings.problem: B1 lemmas; with `zo nu en dan` replaced (L7) the three unglossed ones fill the stretch budget of 3 exactly.
findings.evidence: vocab table ok-stretch / glossed; `Verdomme` is B1 but missing from the table
findings.required_fix: None.

findings.fragment: een spits gezicht
findings.problem: The lexicon knows `spits` as a noun; the adjective 'pointed' is a known word in a new sense, and the standard word for Draco's face.
findings.evidence: lexicon: spits known A2 NOUN
findings.required_fix: Keep. Lexicon owner: add the ADJ sense.

flag_decisions.reason: `verbaasd` is a lexicon adjective (A1) used attributively in `een licht verbaasde blik`; restricted.md names it explicitly as fine. No clause is being replaced.
`volgende` is the ordinary adjective 'next' (A1), not a participle phrase.

flag_decisions.span: Nou ja, iedereen wilde toch de hand van Harry Potter schudden, dus — “Als mijn kleren klaar zijn, meneer, wilt u zich dan misschien verwaardigen tot een handdruk?
flag_decisions.reason: The tool merged the narration (`…schudden, dus—`, 1 finite verb) with the quoted question (2 finite verbs, one als-clause) across the em-dash; each unit is within the limits. The dash is in the source.

tool_feedback.reason: amod participle whose lemma is a lexicon ADJ (`verbaasd`, A1) and which restricted.md lists as fine; skip amod participles that are lexicon adjectives, or lower them below ignore_confidence.
`volgend(e)` is a lexicalised adjective; add it (with `vorige`, `komende`) to a skip list.
sentence segmentation joins narration and the quoted sentence across `dus—“`; split at an opening quote after a dash.

tool_feedback.item: load b062 em-dash aside not reported
tool_feedback.reason: `Een van de assistentes—zij herkende …, zo leek het—maakte …` has 3 finite verbs and a 9-word subject–verb gap; a parenthetical main clause between subject and verb deserves an L-NEST/L-FRAME style finding.

tool_feedback.item: vocab `zo nu en dan` (b055) not surfaced
tool_feedback.reason: the phrase is stretch B1 in lexicon.phrases, but vocab_check only applies phrases with status known; stretch/hard phrases should be reported as lemmas.
transparent compound/loanwords; they alone produce the density FAIL (14.2/1000) and the b055 cluster — after dismissal 2 unglossed new lemmas = 5.7/1000, within limits.
the same two tokens are listed as ADJ `verrukt` and VERB `verrukken`.
transparent compound of `hand` + `druk` (both A1); B2 overstates it, though glossing is still right.

tool_feedback.item: vocab `Verdomme` (b066) and `Oeps` (b064) absent from the table
tool_feedback.reason: sentence-initial capital → spaCy PROPN → counted as a name; `verdomme` is stretch B1 and counts against the budget, `oeps` is not in the lexicon at all (add as known interjection).
separable `terugkaatsen` not recomposed; the @glosses line names `terugkaatsen`, so gloss matching worked by surface form only.
all matched a known entry of a different sense; the tool cannot see known-word-new-meaning cases (idea.md §4), so the reviewer has to.
